U1_DECISION.decision: Do not choose an invalid owner to satisfy a requested freeze. No responsibility-preserving existing-table representation has been demonstrated. This is not a mathematical impossibility claim.

necessary_record.scope: TEXT NOT NULL; server-derived authorization namespace, never trust caller scope alone
necessary_record.commandKind: TEXT NOT NULL; versioned endpoint dictionary
necessary_record.callerKey: TEXT NOT NULL; immutable caller identity
necessary_record.actorId: TEXT NOT NULL FK User(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
necessary_record.requestHash: CHAR(64) NOT NULL; lowercase SHA-256 of canonical actor, kind, scope, payload and expected versions
necessary_record.expectedVersions: Canonical resource-ID to decimal BIGINT string map; typed subject links also required, not JSON-only relationships
necessary_record.outcome: TEXT NOT NULL CHECK IN ('SUCCEEDED','REJECTED'); terminal only
necessary_record.httpStatus: INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK BETWEEN 100 AND 599; terminal endpoint dictionary further limits valid combinations
necessary_record.frozenResponse: Exact original status/body and generated identifiers; retain original serialized body bytes or immutable canonical bytes with versioned serializer, not current-state reconstruction

necessary_record.subject_links: Typed nullable FK columns with explicit shape checks; rejection of missing target has no target FK, but actor/root receipt identity must still exist; arbitrary multi-resource root mapping remains missing

U1_DECISION.identity: UNIQUE(scope, commandKind, callerKey), independent of requestHash. Current operationIdentity hashes tuple into r6 key; retain full tuple too, never replace authoritative tuple uniqueness with only a digest.
U1_DECISION.canonicalization: Preserve array order, sort object keys, reject undefined/NaN/unsafe numbers, encode exact decimals and versions as strings; use current inventory-core canonical helper as reference. Freeze Unicode/decimal normalization and endpoint-specific semantic fields before adapter implementation.
U1_DECISION.retention: Append terminal records without fixed slot count or TTL for business-history lifetime, including no-ops and required business rejections. RESTRICT deletes/updates of identity, hash, response and links. Retire principals by deactivation or retention-safe pseudonymization preserving IDs. Never store tokens, passwords or raw secrets in responses. Response size and memory-erasure/receipt-PII policy still require field-level resolution; do not silently truncate receipts.
U1_DECISION.rejections: Authenticate/current-authorize first. Retain deterministic authorized domain failures: invalid domain input, not found, stale versions, insufficient eligible stock, invalid lifecycle and expired/revoked/stale approval. Auth failures outside command boundary, malformed uncanonicalizable envelopes, same-key/hash conflict, deadlock/serialization/connection failures are not new terminal receipts. Conflict must not overwrite original receipt.

WRITER_MATRIX.ownership_rule: All stock effects enter Inventory boundary, all customer money enters Payments, purchasing through Purchasing, genuine Agent rows through Agent. No direct repository/worker/seed side door. Exact source hits below include raw SQL candidates; static regex cannot certify dynamically constructed writes or runtime ACL enforcement.

TRANSACTION_MODEL.adapter: Select awaited row-level repository methods in one PostgreSQL transaction; no synchronous getters backed by lazy Prisma, whole-state flush, mock FIFO or callback publication. Backend+Agent consume uses one connection and transaction-scoped unit of work. Real LLM/payment/email dispatch outside SQL transaction with durable intent/result ownership first, currently incomplete.
TRANSACTION_MODEL.isolation: READ COMMITTED with mandatory protected parent/range locks and fresh reads after waits; all relevant insert/update paths participate. SERIALIZABLE may supplement but never replaces receipt owner/uniqueness. Client connection pinned; timeouts explicit; confirmed serialization/deadlock rollback retry max three total attempts.
TRANSACTION_MODEL.lock_order: Current User authority rows sorted -> scoped command transaction advisory lock -> genuine AgentExecution -> ranked parents Order, PurchaseRequest, StockCount, GoodsReceipt -> Product/Recipe/Topping -> Supplier/SupplierIngredient -> Ingredient -> IngredientBatch -> allocation events -> Payment -> Callback. Within rank sort IDs. Discover full set then revalidate under locks; late lower-rank discovery rolls back/replans, never acquires reverse order. Transfers lock both PRs before stock. Role updates lock same authority row. Actual all-writer trace and deadlock tests remain required.
TRANSACTION_MODEL.key_lock: Transaction-scoped advisory lock derived deterministically from full unique scope/kind/key, acquired before savepoint. Hash collisions serialize unrelated keys harmlessly; authoritative full-tuple unique constraint still required. One root command per transaction; child commands use deterministic typed identities, not independently acquired root locks.
savepoint_rejection_steps: BEGIN; lock current authority, authorize; acquire scoped key lock; fresh authoritative receipt SELECT; compare hash or replay before effects.
If absent: SAVEPOINT business_effects. Execute domain validation/effects and all Agent/stock writes in that subtransaction.

On recognized deterministic business error: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT business_effects, restoring all effects. Capture immutable error code/status/body in process before rollback. Locks acquired after savepoint may be released, so required key/authority locks must precede it.

Write terminal rejection receipt AFTER ROLLBACK TO, in surviving outer transaction; no success receipt written inside rolled-back effects. RELEASE SAVEPOINT; validate remaining constraints; COMMIT outer transaction.

On success: RELEASE SAVEPOINT; write exact success receipt in outer transaction; force deferred constraints before commit as appropriate. Any infrastructure or uncategorized/deferred integrity error rolls back whole transaction; never fabricate domain rejection for unknown database failure.

Send result only after outer commit or authoritative lookup. Crash before commit rolls back effects and receipt; crash after durable commit retains both. Recognized integrity failures requiring retained rejection must be checked/mapped inside savepoint before its release, not discovered only at COMMIT.
TRANSACTION_MODEL.savepoint_proof: ROLLBACK TO removes writes after named savepoint; terminal receipt inserted afterward belongs to surviving outer transaction and persists only if outer COMMIT succeeds. Therefore effect rollback and receipt retention are compatible. Current mock models that order, but no PostgreSQL table can receive the receipt yet. This proves SQL control-flow property only, not U1 storage legitimacy or durability.
unknown_commit_steps: Connection/commit acknowledgement loss -> UNKNOWN, never inferred rollback. Preserve exact original key/payload/hash/versions; do not execute command effects again.

Open recovery transaction on authoritative writable primary for same durable database incarnation; current-authorize before exposing response; acquire same transaction key lock with bounded wait. Original transaction still holding it -> wait/UNKNOWN, no negative lookup claim.

After lock acquired, run a new READ COMMITTED SELECT of immutable full-tuple receipt. Matching hash -> original response; differing hash -> 409; never recompute from mutable domain state. No replica or old snapshot for negative lookup.

Absence proves original local transaction did not commit only if every writer holds key lock through commit, effects+receipt are atomic, no bypass/prepared transaction/failover data loss/retention deletion exists and authoritative recovery is established. Otherwise remain UNKNOWN. Lock acquisition alone is not proof if any condition is unproven.

For this source boundary, return UNKNOWN when receipt absent; current BusinessWorkflows already does this. Any later certified rollback retry stays within three confirmed attempts. Provider-side UNKNOWN requires separate merchant lookup and cannot be cleared by local receipt absence.
TRANSACTION_MODEL.child_identity: Root plus OrderItem/source component/Ingredient/Batch/phase/ordinal; inventory-core.childKey(batchId) alone collides when two items share batch and must not become durable unique identity.

steps: M0: Stop at U1. Obtain responsibility-preserving physical owner proof satisfying rejected creation, unlimited history and multi-resource root; freeze missing U2-U5 owners and complete field/FK/check dictionary. No connection or migration in this task.

M1: Prepare new versioned nonexecuted additive Prisma/SQL artifacts, never rewrite applied historical migrations. Preserve exact final table/enum identities and labels. Separate SQL-only partial/exclusion/deferred/privilege rules from Prisma declarations; no unapproved extension assumed.

M2: Replace unsafe migration_27_tables scripts. 00_precheck/03_verify currently write backup tables; new inspection must be read-only. 01_expand status/FK differences require explicit mapping; 04 CASCADE and 05 destructive resets rejected. No auxiliary runtime persistence introduced.

M3: With separate authorization, inspect isolated catalog/ACLs read-only and compare source/generated client/SQL; establish exact starting version before any DDL. Validate lock/function/grant plan and all T01-T36 under runtime roles in disposable PostgreSQL.

M4: Build reviewed preservation mapping for legacy IDs, units, Product->Ingredient origins, nullable actor/cost, lots/ledger, singular->many payments and Agent evidence. Unknown mappings block affected rows/cutover, never invent provenance or default unknown cost to zero. Authoritative audit inventory stays an offline artifact, not extra target table.

M5: Add/backfill/validate under separately authorized migration. Choose controlled write quiescence for final conversion: stop API mutations/workers/seeds, drain in-flight transactions and provider dispatches, establish backup+WAL watermark. Do not dual-write incompatible legacy and target balances. Large backfill chunked with exact reconciliation and FK validation.

M6: Implement awaited adapters and migrate every listed caller; compile generated client/shared DTOs; run project-defined full tests/build plus isolated database acceptance. Application source implementation is a later task, not done by this design artifact.

M7: Only after explicit cutover authorization: atomic writer/grant switch, final parity/count/conservation check, enable target-only writers, retain recoverable old data offline. Retire exactly Inventory/InventoryBatch/SupplierProduct/AgentLog with enumerated dependency removal, no CASCADE. Final catalog must equal target 27/16.

M8: Observe with read-only reconciliation; keep UNKNOWN operations unresolved until authoritative lookup; verify restart/replay and backup+later-write recovery. No weekly/full acceptance gate cleared before actual evidence.
R0 current task: documentation only; no database state to undo. Preserve pre-existing dirty worktree. No staging/commit/push.

R1 before cutover/no target writes: retain additive data/DDL, keep target disabled. Revert application feature switch only if old writer/data contract remains valid; do not run blanket DELETE/reset rollback.

R2 after target writes: quiesce target mutations/dispatch; preserve immutable operation keys/results, stock history, approvals, callbacks and provider truth. Do not restart legacy writers unless lossless reverse mapping of every later write is proven. Prefer roll-forward fix; incompatible rollback stays blocked.

R3 catastrophic recovery: restore validated backup plus WAL/PITR through required durable watermark into isolated recovery target; reconcile external provider effects and dedup identities before switching traffic. Restore of backup alone discarding later writes is unacceptable.

R4 after legacy retirement: use tested backup/WAL and reviewed mapping; no CASCADE recreation shortcut, no reset PAID/refunded states, no synthesized Agent/stock history. Re-run parity/conservation/replay checks before unquiescing.
R5 if command receipts or provider dispatch intent cannot be recovered exactly: remain stopped/UNKNOWN; never compensate by blind re-execution or fake stock return.
